Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal This Criminal Appeal is filed under Section 372 of Cr.P.C. by the appellant being aggrieved of judgment dated 29.08.2024 passed by learned 8 th Additional Sessions Judge, Sagar district Sagar (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No. 34 of 2020, whereby learned trial Court has acquitted all the five accused persons from the charges under Section 498-A & 304-B of Indian Penal Code.

The deceased died on 26.11.2019, i.e., within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage.
It is alleged that she was subjected to cruelty on account of demand of dowry and that her death NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17006 2 CRA-12844-2024 occurred as a consequence thereof.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records, it is not disputed that deceased Chhita @ Sita was taken to the hospital on 26.11.2019, where she died during treatment on account of consumption of Zinc Phosphite.

Mother of the deceased Sita namely Rakkhi Ahirwar (PW-2), father Makhan Baratha (PW-3) and sister Malti Ahirwar (PW-4) expressed that, accused had given her poison, whereas Jassu Ahirwar (PW-5) expressed that, deceased had consumed Rat Killer as a result of which, she died.
5. It has come on record that there is no iota of evidence to suggest that, rat killer was administered by the accused persons to the deceased Chhita @ Sita.

It has also come on record and stated by Dr.
R.S. Bhojak (PW-6) that, deceased Sita was brought to the hospital for treatment by her husband.
Husband of Sita had informed Dr. Bhojak that Sita had consumed some poisonous substance.
When Sita was brought to him, she was conscious.
At about 03:00 Pre-MLC was prepared which does not make mention of any fact that accused had administered poisonous substance to Sita.

6. On 26.11.2019 only upon getting information about illness of Sita, her parental side witnesses had reached Hospital at Sagar but they never NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17006 3 CRA-12844-2024 gave any statement to the police that Sita was administered poison.
In the Out Patient Department record of the District Hospital Sagar, it is clearly mentioned that Sita was brought by Diwan Ahirwar.
7. In the postmortem report (Ex.P-7) carried out by Dr. Jitendra Singh (PW-10), it is mentioned that cause of death was Cardio-respiratory failure.
FIR (Ex.P-6) was lodged on 05.12.2019, in which it is mentioned that, complainant is Sita @ Chhita Ahirwar through Amrita Diwakar, CSP Makroniya.
In the FIR (Ex.P-6) it is mentioned that, after marriage she was being harassed for demand of dowry and therefore, she had filed a case for maintenance in the competent Court.
She had also recorded a report at earlier point of time at Police Station Banda.
8. FSL Report is Ex.P-9, which makes a mention of the fact that Zinc Phosphite was found in the body of the deceased.

Report lodged by Sita at Police Station Mandar, registering case crime No.
307/2019 under Section 498A, 294, 323, 506 & 34 of IPC is available on record against Diwan Ahirwar, husband of the deceased, father-in-law Madan Ahirwar and mother-in-law Rajrani Ahirwar.
Thus, it is evident that, no report was lodged at earlier point of time against Lakhan and Rahul.

9. Rakkhi (PW-2) mother of the deceased admitted that at earlier point of time, there was a dispute,
compromise was affected at Mahila Police Station.
Police personnel had affected that compromise and thereafter, In- charge of Mahila Police Station had sent Sita to her in-law's house.

This witness has expressed innocence to the suggestion that Sita was fighting with her family members and was running away from her matrimonial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17006 4 CRA-12844-2024 home.
She pleads ignorance that Diwan had lodged a report that Sita used to abscond leaving him behind.

She further admits that complainant party had informed her that on 25.11.2019 Sita had informed her mother Rakkhi over phone that accused party had administered something,
but she had not investigated the mobile numbers and call details.
She admits that except for the family members of the deceased, she had not recorded the statements of any of the neighbors in regard to harassment of Sita.
17. Kiran Batke (PW-13) is the person who had recorded earlier FIR on 16.04.2019, she admits that it was written on the basis of a written complaint.

18. It has come on record and not disputed that Sita was not having any mobile, therefore,
confession of her mother Rakkhi (PW-2) that she had received a phone call from Sita when Sita had informed her about administration of rat poison by accused party is not proved.
It has come on record that, compromise was affected without any pressure or coercion.
19. It has also come on record that, Sita used to run away to her maika without informing her husband who was residing separately from his parents.

There is evidence of Mamta Athya (DW-1),
Sarpanch of Grampanchayat Pipariya Chamari that Panchayat was convened by Diwan, where in,
Diwan had, alleged harassment in the hands of Sita @ Chhita, when Panchanama (Ex.D-2) was recorded on 16.02.2018.
It was signed by all the panches of the village and Panchayat had counselled Sita to not to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17006 7 CRA-12844-2024 harass Diwan.
Nothing substantial has come in the cross-examination of this witness.
20. Diwan Ahirwar (DW-2) husband of Sita proved Ex.D-3 & Ex.D- 4, documents pertaining to compromise.
Ex.D-3 is the judgment dated 30.09.2019 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Banda in Cr. Case No. 429 of 2019.

This case was decided on merits after reaching a conclusion that, prosecution failed to prove its case and therefore, accused persons were acquitted from the charges under Section 498-A, 498-A/34 and 294 of IPC.
It has come on record in para-7 of this judgment dated 30.09.2019 that there was no material in regard to physical or mental torture being meted out the complainant Sita.

21. When these facts are taken into consideration, then it is evident that Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gurucharan Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2017)1 SCC 433, has held that proof of the willful conduct actuating the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health, whether mental or physical, is the sine qua non for entering a finding of cruelty against the person charged.

All the safeguards and the jurisprudential values of criminal law, are intended to prevent any failure of justice.

In the backdrop of foregoing discussion and the legal principles laid down in the aforementioned cases, it is found that the acquittal of the present respondent rests on cogent and well-reasoned grounds, warranting no interference.
We are of the considered view that the acquittal of respondents is based on sound legal reasonings.
No perversity or illegality is committed while passing the impugned judgment of acquittal.
24. Accordingly, this Criminal Appeal fails and is dismissed.

Our criminal jurisprudence is essentially based on the promise that no innocent shall be condemned as guilty.
The principles which come into play while deciding an appeal from acquittal could be summarised as :
(i) Appreciation of evidence is the core element of a criminal trial and such appreciation must be comprehensive -- inclusive of all evidence, oral or documentary;
(ii) Partial or selective appreciation of evidence may result in a miscarriage of justice and is in itself a ground of challenge;
(iii) If the court, after appreciation of evidence, finds that two views are possible, the one in favour of the accused shall ordinarily be followed;
(iv) If the view of the trial court is a legally plausible view, mere possibility of a contrary view shall not justify the reversal of acquittal;
(v) If the appellate court is inclined to reverse the acquittal in appeal on a reappreciation of evidence, it must specifically address all the reasons given by the trial court for acquittal and must cover all the facts;
